Paulding County, Georgia: Your Guide to Tax Sales

Thinking about buying property through a tax sale in Paulding County, Georgia? You’re not alone. These sales can be a smart way to invest in real estate at a lower cost—if you know what you’re doing. This guide breaks it all down in plain English, with updated links and useful tips to help you make smart decisions.

Quick Table: Paulding County Tax Sale Details

How the Paulding County Tax Sale Works

Tax deed sales in Georgia are held on the first Tuesday of every month. The auction is a public outcry sale, where the highest bidder wins and must pay right away using certified funds.

If you win the bid, you’ll receive a tax deed. But be aware—the original owner has 12 months to redeem the property. They can reclaim it by paying you the full auction amount plus 20% interest for the first year and 10% interest for each subsequent year.

Registration Process

You must register before the auction to be allowed to bid. The required documents and deadlines are usually listed in the public notice for each sale. You can also confirm details by contacting the Paulding County Tax Commissioner.

Auction Location

Tax sales are usually held in front of the:

Paulding County Courthouse
240 Constitution Boulevard
Dallas, GA 30132

Always double-check the public notice to confirm the exact time and location.

Pro Tips for Tax Sale Investors in Paulding

  • Focus on properties near schools—they tend to have higher demand.
  • Ask if there are any active land leases on the property.
  • Always check for road access. Some properties don’t have legal entry points.
  • Use GIS tools and county maps to research before bidding.

Why Paulding County Is a Great Place to Invest

Paulding County sits on the western edge of metro Atlanta and includes cities like Dallas and Hiram. This area is growing fast thanks to affordable housing, large lots, and its small-town feel.

Residents enjoy outdoor spaces like the Silver Comet Trail, which runs through Paulding and offers great opportunities for walking, running, and biking.

Other attractions include:

  • Paulding County Sports Complex
  • Dallas Landing Park (near Lake Allatoona)
  • Golf at Bentwater and Creekside Golf Clubs

Add in good schools, community events, and easy access to Atlanta, and you’ve got a strong foundation for investment.

What Makes Paulding County Tax Sales Worth It?

  • High-Interest Returns: 20% interest return if the property is redeemed within the first year.
  • Low Entry Point: Properties often sell for far below market value.
  • Public Access: Sales are open to all, even out-of-state and international investors.
  • Over-the-Counter Options: Properties not sold at auction may be available directly from the county later.

What If the Property Isn’t Redeemed?

If the former owner doesn’t redeem the property within 12 months, you may gain full ownership through a process called “barment.” This involves notifying the previous owner and other interested parties that you’re cutting off their redemption rights, as outlined under Georgia law.

FAQs – Paulding County Tax Deed Sales

Can I inspect the property before bidding?
Yes, but only from the outside. You can’t enter the home or lot.

What if the original owner redeems the property?
You’ll get back your bid plus the 20% interest. It’s still a good return.

Do I get a warranty deed?
No. You’ll receive a tax deed, which may require a quiet title action if you want to resell or finance the property.

Are these auctions held online?
Not right now. Tax sales are held in person at the courthouse.

Can foreign investors participate?
Yes. Georgia does not restrict tax sales to in-state buyers. It’s open to everyone.

Paulding County, GA – At A Glance

Final Thoughts

Tax deed sales in Paulding County offer a way to invest in property with strong upside potential. If you take time to research, register properly, and understand the redemption rules, you could walk away with a solid investment—whether it’s returned with interest or you end up owning the property.

Pro Tips Recap

  • Drive by the property before bidding.
  • Check public records for liens or title issues.
  • Make sure there’s road access and legal zoning for your goals.
  • Always read the legal notices carefully.
